ask.prompt:
A B2B company sells to enterprises. Work out how its buyers research on the internet before they ever contact a vendor.

Company: DukaanLens (https://khushboo02verma.github.io/dukaanlens/)
What it sells: Out-of-stock detection; Share of shelf measurement; Planogram compliance check; Price label check; Shelf-audit dashboard by store, area and distributor
In one line: A shelf-audit tool for FMCG sales teams. A salesman photographs a kirana store shelf in the app, and computer vision reports out-of-stocks, share of shelf, planogram compliance and price-label mismatches.
Ideal buyer: FMCG brands (biscuits and snacks, beverages, personal care) that sell through Indian kirana stores and have a field sales team. The site gives no company size. Buyers named: sales heads (main), trade marketing managers and category managers (share-of-shelf page).
Country: India
Known rivals: Trax, Pensa Systems, Bizom, ParallelDots (ShelfWatch), Infilect

How enterprise buying works now: something happens (an incident, an audit finding, a customer mandate, a board question) and a manager is told to act. They usually do not know what the solution is called. Most first describe the problem to an AI assistant in their own words. Once they have vocabulary they run a few short Google searches, read the AI Overview, watch a video. Because the ticket is large they then look for several companies to compare, and check each name before contacting anyone.

Write the searches as that buyer would, not as a marketer would. Problem words before product words. No brand names except in "shortlist" comparisons.

Finish with one ```json block:
{
  "category": ["2 or 3 names the buyer will learn this category is called"],
  "triggers": [{"event": "what happened", "who": "role told to act", "why": "one line: which evidence shows this happens to buyers like these, and how often"}],

  "frame": ["8 questions typed to an AI assistant by someone who does not know the category yet; 10 to 25 words, plain, specific to their plant or business"],
  "explore": ["12 short Google searches of 2 to 5 words made after they learn the vocabulary"],
  "shortlist": ["8 Google searches made to find and compare vendors, such as best ... companies in <country>, ... vendors, A vs B"],
  "shortlistQuestions": ["4 questions to an AI assistant asking which companies to consider"],
  "rivalDomains": {"Rival name": "theirsite.com"}
}
"share" values add up to 1. 4 to 6 triggers, 3 to 5 roles.
ask.answer:
**How these buyers research:** An FMCG sales head sees a gap between what salesmen report and what secondary sales show. The gap might be a dip in a region, a distributor dispute, or a retailer ignoring a display agreement. They first ask an AI assistant how to check shelves without visiting every store. They learn the terms "shelf audit", "share of shelf" and "planogram compliance", then run short searches. Because a rollout across a field force is a large commitment, they compare vendors, mostly those with Indian kirana experience.
